liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playing In The Band** (3 reviews): Opening the first set, Playin' came out shorter than a post-warm-up second-set version would have; A Playin' into Crazy Fingers opening was unusual and not the norm for the band [23][30][32]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): As a first-set opener, Crazy Fingers was also shorter than it would have been later in the show [23]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Opening the second set, it was revitalized compared with the slow versions played since the late 1970s [23]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Eyes Of The World is called sloppy, but the post-Space Dear Mr Fantasy section is described as monstrous [32]
- **Dear Mr Fantasy** (1 review): The reviewer calls the Dear Mr Fantasy into Hey Jude sequence the best ever played, with extremely high energy [24]
- **How Y'All Doin'** (1 review): Jerry stepped to the mike early on and asked how everyone was doing, which reviewer later learned was rare [34]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-07-02.138306.mtx.miller.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 159 min; rated 4.4/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1989-07-02.fob.nak300.andrewf.99912.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 158 min [3]
- **gd1989-07-02.fob.nak300.andrewf.99911.flac24**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 158 min [4]
- **gd1989-07-02.153412.MTX.photoLeon.t-flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 162 min [5]. Said about its sound: Eyes Of The World is missing vocals from 00:13 to 00:49 [5]
- **gd89-07-02.nak.8243.sbefail.shnf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 165 min; rated 4.1/5 by 30 [10]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording quality just okay [32]

## Around the show

- Reviewer paid $90 to a ticket agency for one general admission ticket, then drove an hour through miles of backed-up traffic [27]
- The parking lot scene was wild, with tons of colorful, smiling people [27]
- Fans with handmade fake mail-order tickets were turned away, since the real tickets had multi-colored paper inside [28]
- It was a miserably humid day, with heat stroke common and fire hoses turned on the crowd [30]
- Day was sunny but hot and humid; people near the front mostly sat on the ground [34]
- Reviewer missed earlier mail-order tickets that had song names and funny sayings showing under black lights [28]
- Reviewer suggests this may be the best show of the summer [29]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-07-02.138306.mtx.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Ultra Matrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [1]. Also: Two sets of master tapes were combined to make the show complete; This is a matrix release converted from a 24-bit version to 16-bit [1]
- **gd1989-07-02.fob.nak300.andrewf.99912.flac16**: taped by Andrew F.; transferred by Andrew F.; source: FOB AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's with no Dolby. Mics on 8-foot stand, approx 10 feet in front of SBD area and 15 feet to… [3]. Also: A patch from another source, ID-8243, covers the Drums section from 03:12 to 03:17; The second set disc break is seamless [3]
- **gd1989-07-02.fob.nak300.andrewf.99911.flac24**: taped by Andrew F.; transferred by Andrew F.; source: FOB AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns FOB AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's with no Dolby. Mics on 8-foot stand, approx 10 feet… [4]. Also: A patch from source ID-8243 was inserted in Drums between 03:12 and 03:17 [4]
- **gd1989-07-02.153412.MTX.photoLeon.t-flac16**: source: A photoLeon Matrix [5]. Also: Joe Noel made the matrix in Adobe Audition from Ted Mattes' FOB recording and Charlie Miller's board source [5]
- **gd89-07-02.nak.8243.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Jill and Rob R; source: 3 Nak CM 300's - 2 CP 4's (Shotguns) 1 CP3 ( Super Omni ) arranged in an X-Y pattern [10]. Also: Uploader has a Schoeps spaced omni source, but could not post it to the archive and offered copies by email [29]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Sullivan Stadium - July 2, 1989](https://www.dead.net/show/july-2-1989) [36]
- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1989-07-02 Sullivan Stadium, Foxboro, MA](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/02/grateful-dead-1989-07-02-sullivan.html) [37]

claims.text: Opening the first set, Playin' came out shorter than a post-warm-up second-set version would have
As a first-set opener, Crazy Fingers was also shorter than it would have been later in the show
Opening the second set, it was revitalized compared with the slow versions played since the late 1970s
The reviewer calls the Dear Mr Fantasy into Hey Jude sequence the best ever played, with extremely high energy
Reviewer paid $90 to a ticket agency for one general admission ticket, then drove an hour through miles of backed-up traffic
The parking lot scene was wild, with tons of colorful, smiling people
Fans with handmade fake mail-order tickets were turned away, since the real tickets had multi-colored paper inside
Reviewer missed earlier mail-order tickets that had song names and funny sayings showing under black lights
Uploader has a Schoeps spaced omni source, but could not post it to the archive and offered copies by email
Reviewer suggests this may be the best show of the summer
A Playin' into Crazy Fingers opening was unusual and not the norm for the band
It was a miserably humid day, with heat stroke common and fire hoses turned on the crowd
The unusual song order led to distinctive playing, with different tempo and emphasis in Playin', Crazy Fingers, Friend Of The Devil and He's Gone
Eyes Of The World is called sloppy, but the post-Space Dear Mr Fantasy section is described as monstrous
Reviewer finds the recording quality just okay
Jerry stepped to the mike early on and asked how everyone was doing, which reviewer later learned was rare
Day was sunny but hot and humid; people near the front mostly sat on the ground
Two sets of master tapes were combined to make the show complete
This is a matrix release converted from a 24-bit version to 16-bit
A patch from another source, ID-8243, covers the Drums section from 03:12 to 03:17
The second set disc break is seamless
A patch from source ID-8243 was inserted in Drums between 03:12 and 03:17
Joe Noel made the matrix in Adobe Audition from Ted Mattes' FOB recording and Charlie Miller's board source
Eyes Of The World is missing vocals from 00:13 to 00:49
